title: Anchor benchmark matrix for attention-window sweep and prefill concurrency governor
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a new benchmark matrix and CI gating strategy that exercises: (1) attention window size sweep (8k/16k/32k logical contexts and trimmed attention kernels), (2) kernel selection sensitivity to mixed quantization/sequence-length mixes, and (3) a new prefill->decode concurrency governor to model real-world bursty traffic. The goal is to produce stable anchor baselines (signed hashes + artifact tarball) and lightweight sentinel suites for CI so perf regressions are caught at PR time without running the full matriX. This ticket covers harness changes, new scenario definitions, data seeding for stochastic traces, and automation to produce per-run artifact bundles for triage.
acceptance_criteria: A1: End-to-end harness can launch attention-window sweep scenarios with configurable kernels and quantization variants
A2: Prefill->decode concurrency governor implemented and exposed to harness config (max_prefill_concurrency, decode_budget_ms)
A3: Anchor baselines produced for three representative platforms (a100-40g, h100-80g, t4-16g) with signed lockfiles and artifact bundles uploaded to the perf bucket
A4: CI sentinel job runs within 30 minutes and verifies 95/99 latency quantiles and token throughput against anchors
A5: Documentation and runbook in Confluence with troubleshooting checklist and triage playbook
comments: 2025-02-14 - Aisha Patel: Initial triage. Identified need to expand existing mixbench to support attention-window parameterization and a concurrency governor. High-level design doc linked.

2025-02-18 - Miguel Ortega: Spike results show current kernel selector picks slower attention kernel for 16k sequences when mixed with short sequences due to averaging. Proposing weighted/selective probing.
2025-02-21 - Design review (Liu Zhang): Recommended adding per-cohort kernel probes rather than global probes to avoid cross-workload contamination.

2025-02-25 - Miguel Ortega: Implemented concurrency governor prototype. Local runs (a100) show 8-12% p99 latency improvement under bursty prefill traffic. Opened GH PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4127
2025-02-28 - Performance lead (Hannah Kim): Requested more deterministic seed hashing for trace replay; added artifact lockfile + seed manifest requirement.
2025-03-01 - Miguel Ortega: CI sentinel draft added to .circleci with reduced scenario set. Next: validate runtime-1.20 integration and storage of artifacts to gs://redwood-perf/anchors/ENG-88765/
decision_log: Decision 2025-02-18: Use per-cohort kernel probing (one probe per cohort of similar seq-length and quantization) to reduce noise from mixed workloads.
Decision 2025-02-23: Anchor baselines will be stored as signed tarballs with seed manifest and git-sha; anchor generation runs will require a quorum of two platform runs to accept a new anchor.
Decision 2025-02-27: CI sentinel will use a reduced scenario set (short/long prefills + mid decode) with tightened 95/99 thresholds; full matrix gated to nightly/weekly jobs only.
telemetry_plan: Collect per-request kernel selection tag (kernel_id) and sequence_length_cohort
Export p50/p95/p99 decode latency and token throughput per-cohort
Record prefill queue depth histogram and concurrency governor evictions
Attach run seed hash and git-sha to dashboard for reproducibility
next_steps: (1) Land probe API change in runtime (PR 4127) and add unit tests
(2) Extend mixbench scenario DSL with attention_window and concurrency_governor fields
(3) Run anchors on a100/h100/t4 and publish artifact bundles
(4) Wire CI sentinel to check anchors and post results to perf dashboard
